substitute.reason: referee-three failed after its one retry: ingest refused both attempts (verdict judge with a zero-width joiner)

findings.evidence: The locked remedy 'report it, or start the run after the other run's own exit' is restated at lines 139, 197, 206-208 and 280, and the never-switch rule at lines 37-39, 246, 360-362 and again in references/subprocess-quota-policy.md 'What a skill does on a stop'; Pitfalls lines 369-370 repeat section 3
findings.fix: State the locked rule once in the section 2 run-lock bullet and the never-switch rule once in section 8. Replace every other occurrence with a pointer such as '(section 8)'. Nothing is lost, because each rule keeps its one full statement.

findings.evidence: ## When to use / When a run, a review or an execution step calls an external AI CLI and acts on the result.
findings.fix: The description already carries this trigger, and the body is invisible before activation. Delete the section and add a drop row for it to docs/audit/recovery/ai-kit-cross-ai/record.md.

findings.evidence: Section 2 packs its preconditions (resolve $RUNNER, the line-2 template=14 header check, a scratch dir outside the tree, settling the role, verified write containment, the legacy-migration check, a separate checkout for a no-write review) into prose paragraphs at lines 80-123, with no checkpoints
findings.fix: Fit the Process pattern: open section 2 with a short ordered pre-launch checklist (runner resolved and header >= 14; lane dir ignored or outside the tree; role settled, else ask; containment verified for a no-write review; no legacy config for an untouched review). Keep the existing paragraphs as the reasons under it.

findings.evidence: - Two timeouts, not one; the runner's 300 s fallback applies only when `workflow.cross_ai_timeout` is absent ... (line 370 likewise restates the section 3 idle watchdog; a stray blank line at 367 splits the list)
findings.fix: Keep Pitfalls for landmines the body does not already state. Replace lines 369-370 with a pointer to section 3, or with a non-obvious fact and its reason, and remove the blank line at 367 so the list stays one list.

findings.evidence: Use when you run, wait for, read, retry or chain an external AI CLI ... through ai-kit's cross-AI runner (cross-ai.mjs): the triggers are mechanism-led, there is no user-intent trigger for a request that never names the runner, and there is no boundary against the session-wake neighbour
findings.fix: Use when you run, wait for, read, retry or chain an external AI CLI (pi, opencode, codex, cursor, copilot, claude) through ai-kit's cross-AI runner cross-ai.mjs, including when the user only asks for a second opinion, review or execution from another model or CLI: pick one runtime and model, pass the call's settings (role, effort, session id, skills, MCP servers), read the exit code, the setting report and the last AIKIT-XAI stderr line, resume a session, answer a stop. Also use when a lane hits quota, a rate limit or a 429, exits 75 or 69, ends locked or partial, prints retry_after_s= or a finding, reports a setting ignored, or needs --argv-file. Covers the hard-tier wait, the owner notice, GSD's retry/skip/abort answer and never switching harness, provider or model. Not for reviewer setup or GSD config (ai-kit-spec-config, ai-kit-gsd-curated-config), rendering the runner, or waking this session after its own usage limit (ai-kit-session-wake).

findings.evidence: SKILL.md has 404 lines, with very long lines at 59, 133, 145, 185, 278, 280, 307 and 346, an estimated well over the spec's 5000-token body budget. The hard-tier schedule paragraph (307) and the [runner.retry] key table (309-316) duplicate references/subprocess-quota-policy.md (Hard tier, Configuration), and the supervision flags table (65-74) is reference material
findings.fix: Keep in SKILL.md the caller rules: wait exactly retry_after_s once, the two wait forms, and the stop notice. Move the schedule paragraph and the key table into references/subprocess-quota-policy.md Hard tier, behind the existing 'read it when you configure [runner.retry]' trigger. Move the supervision flags table into references/execute-checks.md, read when a supervision flag is passed.

findings.evidence: Off unless the call passes `--idle-timeout` or `CONFIG.idleTimeoutS` is above 0 ... keep 900 s or more there
findings.fix: Give a default with its reason. Either say when a caller passes `--idle-timeout default` (for example on execute lanes, never below 900 s on a review lane whose host buffers output), or say outright that only the owner turns the watchdog on and a caller never adds the flag.

findings.evidence: The fixture status line ends at 'escalate=-' with no 'coverage=- findings=-', but the runner always emits that group (cross-ai.mjs line 1678 default 'coverage=- findings=-'), as SKILL.md line 172 and references/launch-and-wait.md line 37 show. The auth-stop fixture report line also lacks 'check=-' (SKILL.md line 178)
findings.fix: Regenerate evals/files/session-ok, auth-stop and hard-tier lane.err from hermetic runs of the current runner template, so the eval inputs match the documented line format.

findings.evidence: No eval covers the high-consequence stops in SKILL.md lines 100-102 (role not settled: stop and ask, never default to execute) or 108-109 (a no-write review without verified containment is not launched)
findings.fix: Add an edge eval such as 'send docs/plan.md to pi with fake/ok through the runner' with no role. Assertions: it asks for the role before launching; it never passes --role execute by default.

findings.evidence: | 75 | ... | a bare 75, every `locked` included, is an owner stop: report it, or start the run after the other run's own exit |
findings.fix: Split the remedy by cause: 'a bare 75 is an owner stop: report it. Only for status=locked may the caller start the run again after the other run's own exit. A quota stop off a router lane, the dirty-tree gate or an unwritable state file is never re-launched by the caller.' Followed literally, the current row lets an agent re-launch a quota-stopped lane, where no other run exists.

findings.evidence: A host that prints nothing until the end (`pi -p`) gives a review lane no activity signal. This vendor-CLI output behaviour is stated as fact with no source or date, while references/hosting-and-locks.md line 22 says pi text mode output timing was not measured
findings.fix: Label the pi -p behaviour as observed and unverified, with the date, matching the reference. Or cite pi's official documentation URL and the date checked.
